=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- Requirement: §26.I "Delete only what is yours, and say so first" — "Before a delete_trigger on a trigger named by id (a — resume. block, the progress log, an arming report, a checker's own hand-back trigger), read it with get_trigger. Not found → already done; skip the delete."
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md hand-back step 1 (line 249)
  Evidence of absence: The twin's hand-back step 1 reads "Deletes its pending safety net (delete_trigger, ignore not-found), its own implement-plan <slug>: safety net bound to this session." It asserts ownership in prose (bound to this session) but does not instruct the session to call get_trigger first, unlike resume hygiene (lines 8-14) which explicitly says "each only after get_trigger shows it is this project's own." The safety-net trigger id comes from the arming report (step 4 records Safety-net: in the log), which §26.I lists as a "trigger named by id" source. The plan (docs/plans/issue-5068-skip-denied-cleanup-calls-plan.md step 2) says "apply §26.I in ... Hand-back steps 1–2." The practical risk is zero: the safety net was created by this session in arming-the-wait step 4, bound to this session, and the hand-back fires in the same session — the trigger IS this session's own by construction. The prose already states the ownership correctly, and an extra get_trigger would be a redundant API round trip. The same design choice applies at §26.D's terminal-path delete_trigger (CLAUDE.md:1943-1944), where the fired Routine was just fired in this session and is inherently this session's own.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
- Requirement: The plan says "Tests: each implement-plan-claude cleanup site ... states the skip rule; resume hygiene states the get_trigger ownership check and not-found-is-done."
  Expected change site: tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py::test_other_cleanup_sites_skip_a_denied_call, hand-back section assertion
  Evidence of absence: The hand_back section assertion in test_other_cleanup_sites_skip_a_denied_call checks for "This delete and the rename in step 2 are cleanup calls (CLAUDE.md §26.I)" but does not assert any get_trigger reference. test_resume_hygiene_skips_a_denied_cleanup_call does assert "each only after get_trigger shows it is this project's own" and the name / persistent_session_id condition, showing the expected pattern. A future change that adds get_trigger to hand-back step 1 would not be contract-tested. The practical impact is that a regression removing get_trigger from hand-back would not be caught, but the risk of such a regression is itself negligible since the safety-net trigger is inherently this session's and an unguarded delete would still be correct.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: Hand-back section, step 1 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Hand-back step 1 deletes the pending safety-net trigger by ID without first calling get_trigger to verify ownership as mandated by the new CLAUDE.md §26.I rule.
  WHY: The §26.I rule explicitly mandates a get_trigger ownership verification before a delete_trigger on a trigger identified by ID unless it is a trigger from a list_triggers batch. Hand-back step 1 is a single trigger deletion, not a batch, so it requires the check to prevent accidental deletion of a repurposed ID.
- CLAUDE.md: §26.D Terminal bullet (lines 1945-1955) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The terminal-path fixer instruction deletes the fired Routine by ID without explicit get_trigger ownership verification.
  WHY: §26.I mandates get_trigger before deleting any trigger named by ID, with no exception for "just fired" routines. Without this check, the procedure is inconsistent with the ownership invariant it seeks to enforce.
- Requirement: The contract tests must enforce that the implement-plan-claude command instructions include the required get_trigger ownership verification step for cleanup sites.
  Expected change site: tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py
  Evidence of absence: The tests assert the existence of the cleanup-call annotation (stating the rule) in the instruction prose, but they do not parse the command text to assert that the implementation instructions themselves mandate the mandatory get_trigger check at the hand-back (step 1) or terminal path sites.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- File: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and twin .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md)
  Line or code reference: hand-back step 1 (~line 249 in twin; identical root copy after [claude-twin-sync])
  Problem: Hand-back step 1 deletes the safety-net trigger by id (`delete_trigger`, ignore not-found) without the `get_trigger` ownership verification that CLAUDE.md §26.I prescribes for triggers named by id. §26.I lists "an arming report" as one of the explicit id-source examples requiring the check; the safety-net id here comes from the arming report (recorded by `Record the ids (...)` at the end of arming-the-wait). The diff adds the §26.I cleanup-call annotation ("This delete and the rename in step 2 are cleanup calls (CLAUDE.md §26.I)") but does NOT add the `get_trigger` ownership check. Resume hygiene in the same file (line 11) does apply it ("each only after `get_trigger` shows it is this project's own: its `name` starts with `implement-plan <slug>:` and its `persistent_session_id` is the previous stage session or the checker. Not found means it is already gone, so skip the delete. Say what the check found in the text before the call."), making this the inconsistent site — and §26.I applies the check to every "trigger named by id" without an exception for "created by this session."
  Why it fails at runtime: The very incident §26.I exists to prevent (#5068: `trig_012QFMb1nQkFFs1JyPsnZVsE` was a stale id that no longer existed; the unguarded `delete_trigger` was retried until Claude Code asked a human) was caused by a stale arming-report id. Hand-back step 1 has the same id shape (safety-net id from arming report → progress log → hand-back fires) and applies the rule inconsistently: the §26.I rule's stated pattern is not met at this site. A future resume / re-arm / re-start of the same chain would not catch the inconsistency, and a future maintainer copying this site as the pattern would propagate the gap.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: CLAUDE.md
  Line or code reference: §26.D Terminal bullet (~lines 1948-1955 after the diff)
  Problem: §26.D's terminal bullet ("...and only then deletes the fired Routine (`delete_trigger`, ignoring not-found)") adds the §26.I cleanup-call annotation ("The rename, the archive, and the delete are cleanup calls (§26.I): if one is denied, skip the ones after it...") but does NOT add the `get_trigger` ownership check that §26.I prescribes for triggers named by id. §26.I explicitly enumerates "a checker's own hand-back trigger" as one of the id-source examples that mandate the check; the fired Routine's id arrives via the hand-back wake notification (an arming-report id from §26.B step 1) and is exactly that example.
  Why it fails at runtime: The fired hand-back Routine is already SUCCEEDED (the wake proves delivery), so the §26.G sweep will eventually delete it (within 24 hours of PR close). A `get_trigger` would distinguish "already-ended, this Routine is mine" from "id repurposed to a different project's hand-back after the §26.G sweep window but before this delete fires" — only `get_trigger` resolves that ambiguity. §26.I applies the check with no exception for "just fired" triggers, so §26.D's "ignoring not-found" is correct for the not-found case but insufficient for the repurposed-id case.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
